dis-1x01: Sent to investigate an unknown object at the Federation's edge, Shenzhou first officer Michael Burnham encounters T'Kuvma's Klingons and mutinies against Captain Georgiou to strike first.
dis-1x02: Klingon ships and Starfleet clash at the binary stars; Georgiou dies trying to capture T'Kuvma, Burnham kills him, and a court sentences her to life for mutiny.
dis-1x03: Convict Michael Burnham is brought onto the USS Discovery, whose secretive Captain Lorca recruits her for his spore-drive project after a grim visit to the ravaged USS Glenn.
dis-1x04: Tasked with studying the Glenn's captured tardigrade, Burnham learns it can steer through the mycelial network, letting Discovery jump in to save the Corvan II colony from Klingons.
dis-1x05: Taken prisoner by the Klingons, Lorca escapes alongside Lieutenant Ash Tyler and leaves Harry Mudd behind, while Stamets injects tardigrade DNA to spare the ailing Ripper.
dis-1x06: Burnham enters the mind of a bomb-injured Sarek and learns he once picked Spock over her, while Cornwell questions Lorca's fitness and falls into Klingon hands.
dis-1x07: Harry Mudd traps Discovery in a time loop, plotting to sell the ship to the Klingons, and only Stamets remembers each reset well enough to stop him.
dis-1x08: On Pahvo, whose crystal spire could expose cloaked Klingon ships, the planet's peaceful inhabitants enthrall Saru, who sabotages the mission before the Pahvans summon the Klingons themselves.
dis-1x09: Defying orders, Lorca keeps Discovery at Pahvo; Stamets' 133 jumps crack the Klingon cloak and doom Kol's flagship, but the last jump sends the ship astray.
dis-1x10: Stranded in the mirror universe, the crew poses as their Terran counterparts, Burnham assumes command of the ISS Shenzhou, and an unraveling Tyler kills Dr. Culber.
dis-1x11: Ordered to wipe out a rebel base, Burnham tries to spare it, Tyler is unmasked as Voq, and the Terran emperor turns out to be Georgiou.
dis-1x12: Aboard the emperor's flagship, Burnham confides her origin to Georgiou and realizes Lorca is Terran, while Stamets meets Culber in the network and L'Rell purges Voq from Tyler.
dis-1x13: Lorca seizes the emperor's flagship, whose mycelial reactor is poisoning the network; Burnham sides with Georgiou, Lorca dies, and Discovery escapes home with the emperor, nine months late.
dis-1x14: Discovery returns to find the Klingons close to winning the war, and a desperate Starfleet secretly installs the mirror Georgiou as captain for a strike on Qo'noS.
dis-1x15: Refusing to let Georgiou blow up Qo'noS, Burnham hands the bomb's detonator to L'Rell, who uses the threat to unite the Klingons and end the war.
dis-2x01: Captain Pike takes command of Discovery to trace seven red signals, finding the wrecked USS Hiawatha on an asteroid, while Burnham dwells on her estrangement from Spock.
dis-2x02: Discovery reaches Terralysium, a pre-warp colony of humans taken from World War III Earth, where Pike weighs General Order 1 and Tilly's curiosity averts disaster.
dis-2x03: Amanda Grayson brings Spock's psychiatric file aboard, Tilly sees an apparition no one else can, and on Qo'noS L'Rell surrenders her infant son to secure her throne.
dis-2x04: A dying alien sphere traps Discovery to upload its memories, Saru survives a Kelpien change he was taught would kill him, and a spore creature cocoons Tilly.
dis-2x05: Discovery pushes partway into the mycelial network to rescue Tilly, and Stamets finds Culber alive there, while Section 31 joins the hunt for Spock over Pike's objections.
dis-2x06: A signal over Kaminar brings Saru home, where the Ba'ul's long culling of the Kelpiens comes to light and the Red Angel thwarts their attempt at genocide.
dis-2x07: On Vulcan, Burnham learns Amanda has been hiding an incoherent Spock, while Pike and Tyler investigate a time rift over Kaminar that lets a future probe infect Airiam.
dis-2x08: Burnham brings Spock to Talos IV for healing, where he reveals a vision of galactic annihilation and the siblings confront the rift between them; Pike meets Vina again.
dis-2x09: Discovery raids Section 31's headquarters, where Control has killed the admirals, and an infected Airiam turns saboteur until she begs to be ejected into space.
dis-2x10: After learning her parents' murder was tied to a Section 31 time-suit project, Burnham risks her life to lure the Red Angel, who proves to be her mother.
dis-2x11: Reunited with the mother she thought dead, Burnham learns Gabrielle is fighting Control across time, until Control takes over Leland and Gabrielle is snapped back to the future.
dis-2x12: On Boreth, Pike accepts a vision of his own grim fate to win a time crystal, as Burnham and Spock find a Section 31 crew slaughtered by Control.
dis-2x13: Unable to destroy Discovery's sphere data, Burnham readies a time suit to lead the ship into the future, and her crew chooses to follow as Control closes in.
dis-2x14: With Klingon and Kelpien help, Enterprise and Discovery hold off Control while Burnham, the true source of the signals, leads Discovery into the future and Spock stays behind.
dis-3x01: Landing alone in 3188, Burnham falls in with courier Cleveland Booker, learns the Burn has shattered the Federation, and finds a lone loyalist, Sahil, still guarding its flag.
dis-3x02: Discovery crash-lands on an ice world, Saru and Tilly seek help from a hostile mining town until Georgiou intervenes, and Burnham finds them after a year's search.
dis-3x03: Captained by Saru, Discovery finds an isolationist Earth outside the Federation, defuses its feud with raiders from Titan, and meets Adira, a human host to a Trill symbiont.
dis-3x04: Burnham takes Adira to Trill to unlock the symbiont's memories, which reveal Adira's late partner Gray, while Saru hosts a crew dinner that erupts into tension.
dis-3x05: Discovery reaches Federation headquarters and a wary Admiral Vance, then earns its place by helping a stricken seed-vault ship while the enigmatic Kovich interrogates Georgiou.
dis-3x06: Burnham and Georgiou go rogue to free Book from an Emerald Chain labor camp and recover a black box holding Burn clues, costing Burnham her first officer post.
dis-3x07: On Ni'Var, the reunified Vulcan-Romulan world, Burnham argues for access to its Burn research with her mother, now a Qowat Milat nun, as her advocate.
dis-3x08: Discovery accompanies Book to Kwejian, where the Emerald Chain's Osyraa exploits a crop-destroying swarm to pressure his people, while Stamets and Adira keep hunting the Burn's origin.
dis-3x09: With Georgiou's body breaking down, Discovery takes her to Dannus V, where a gatekeeper named Carl sends her back into the mirror universe of her past.
dis-3x10: Reliving her reign in the Terran Empire, Georgiou meets a coup with newfound mercy, then learns Carl is the Guardian of Forever and leaves Discovery for good.
dis-3x11: Inside the Verubin Nebula, Saru, Culber, and Burnham find Su'Kal, a Kelpien raised alone on a wrecked ship, whose anguish caused the Burn, as Osyraa moves on Discovery.
dis-3x12: Osyraa brings the captured Discovery to Federation headquarters and offers Vance an alliance, while Burnham slips back aboard to retake the ship from Emerald Chain forces.
dis-3x13: Burnham retakes Discovery and kills Osyraa, Book steers the spore drive to rescue the away team from the nebula, and Saru steps aside so Burnham can take command.
dis-4x01: Captain Burnham's Discovery rescues a space station damaged by a gravitational anomaly under President Rillak's eye, and the same phenomenon then obliterates Book's homeworld, Kwejian.
dis-4x02: Saru returns to help study the anomaly, and Burnham joins a grieving Book on a flight into it while helping him face the loss of his family.
dis-4x03: Burnham and Tilly pursue a renegade Qowat Milat who killed a Starfleet officer, while Stamets works to predict the anomaly and Gray finally receives a synthetic body.
dis-4x04: Tilly and Adira's cadet training flight crash-lands on a planetoid, Burnham joins Ni'Var's talks on rejoining the Federation, and Tilly decides to leave Discovery to teach.
dis-4x05: As the anomaly nears a stranded colony, Burnham and Book scramble to get everyone out, while the brilliant, abrasive Ruon Tarka joins Saru and Stamets.
dis-4x06: Trapped inside a subspace rift left by the anomaly, Discovery struggles to escape as its AI Zora feels fear and Book sees visions of his father.
dis-4x07: A galactic summit debates attacking or contacting the anomaly's makers, Book and Tarka break ranks, and Kovich tests whether the newly sentient Zora is a threat.
dis-4x08: Guessing Book's next move, Burnham seeks him out at a spot they knew as couriers and gets pulled into a contest over a dangerous weapon.
dis-4x09: With Nhan aboard to keep Burnham in check, Discovery chases Book and Tarka to the anomaly, but their weapon destroys it and Species 10-C promptly makes another.
dis-4x10: Discovery crosses the Galactic Barrier in search of Species 10-C, while Book discovers that Tarka's true goal is to reach another universe and reunite with a lost friend.
dis-4x11: An away team led by Burnham searches the former homeworld of Species 10-C for clues to how they communicate, while Book and Tarka slip aboard Discovery undetected.
dis-4x12: Inside the hyperfield of Species 10-C, Burnham's team attempts first contact through math and chemistry as the anomaly bears down on Earth and Ni'Var.
dis-4x13: With Earth and Ni'Var evacuating, Burnham and Book help Species 10-C grasp the harm their anomaly causes, and the aliens withdraw it as Tarka dies chasing his dream.
dis-5x01: Burnham retrieves an 800-year-old Romulan ship holding a clue to the Progenitors' lost technology, but the couriers Moll and L'ak steal it, sparking a chase.
dis-5x02: Saru's final outing as first officer takes the team to an apparently deserted planet, where they piece together the next clue to the Progenitors' hidden technology.
dis-5x03: On Trill, Culber temporarily hosts the memories of long-dead Jinaal, who puts Burnham and Book through a dangerous test for the next clue, as Adira reunites with Gray.
dis-5x04: A time bug planted by Moll and L'ak flings Discovery through moments from its own past, and only Burnham, Rayner, and Stamets can track the device down.
dis-5x05: Following the clue into extradimensional space, Burnham and Book find Moll and L'ak aboard the derelict ISS Enterprise, while Rayner commands Discovery for the first time.
dis-5x06: Undercover on a pre-warp world, Burnham weighs defying the Prime Directive to save Tilly from a deadly local rite, while Rayner hands Adira a bridge post.
dis-5x07: The Breen demand the fugitives Moll and L'ak, forcing a standoff at Federation Headquarters that ends with L'ak dead and Moll handed over to Primarch Ruhn.
dis-5x08: In an ancient archive, a mindscape tests whether Burnham is worthy of the Progenitors' power, while Book, Rayner, and the crew keep the Breen at bay.
dis-5x09: Burnham's team steals aboard the Breen dreadnought to recover the structure hiding the Progenitors' power, which Moll has helped the Breen capture, before they can unlock it.
dis-5x10: Inside a gravity-bending portal, Burnham battles Moll for the Progenitors' technology and decides no one should wield it, as Rayner leads Discovery against the Breen.
ds9-1x01-02: Still grieving the wife the Borg killed, Commander Sisko takes charge of a gutted Cardassian station over Bajor and finds a stable wormhole, becoming the Bajorans' prophesied Emissary.
ds9-1x03: Kira is torn when former resistance comrade Tahna Los seeks asylum, then buys explosives from Lursa and B'Etor to collapse the wormhole and drive the Federation away.
ds9-1x04: When Ibudan, a criminal Odo once jailed, turns up dead in a locked holosuite, suspicion falls on Odo until he proves the corpse was Ibudan's own clone.
ds9-1x05: An aphasia virus left in a replicator by the Bajoran resistance spreads across the station, scrambling speech, and Kira must track down the scientist who can cure it.
ds9-1x06: O'Brien befriends Tosk, a Gamma Quadrant native bred to be hunted, and bends the rules to free him when his hunters board the station to reclaim him.
ds9-1x07: Vash returns from the Gamma Quadrant with Q in tow, and a gem she means to auction proves to be an embryo pulling the station toward the wormhole.
ds9-1x08: Accused of a decades-old murder her previous host, Curzon, allegedly committed, Jadzia faces extradition and stays silent rather than expose his affair with the victim's wife.
ds9-1x09: Fugitive Rao Vantika fakes his death by hiding his consciousness inside Dr. Bashir, then uses the doctor's body in a bid to hijack a precious deuridium shipment.
ds9-1x10: After Quark cheats the Wadi, the first Gamma Quadrant delegation to visit, they draw him into a game in which Sisko, Kira, Dax, and Bashir become living pieces.
ds9-1x11: Zek names Quark his successor and seemingly dies, making Quark Grand Nagus and a target for Rom and Krax, until Zek reveals it was all a test.
ds9-1x12: Arrested for murder, Gamma Quadrant fugitive Croden tempts Odo with hints about his people, and Odo ultimately lets him flee to protect his daughter.
ds9-1x13: Kai Opaka's runabout crashes on a moon where two factions are revived after every death to fight forever; Opaka is killed, revived, and stays to seek peace.
ds9-1x14: O'Brien is named Sirah of a Bajoran village and must banish the dreaded Dal'Rok, while Jake and Nog befriend Varis, a teenage leader in a land dispute.
ds9-1x15: Kira must uproot Mullibok, an old farmer, from a Bajoran moon about to be tapped for power, while Jake and Nog trade yamok sauce into a land deed.
ds9-1x16: Rumpelstiltskin, ballplayer Buck Bokai, and an adoring Jadzia double appear as the crew's fantasies take form, and even a rift menacing the Bajoran system proves imaginary.
ds9-1x17: A probe from the Gamma Quadrant leaves a playful alien program loose in the station's computer, trapping Odo in a stalled turbolift with a smitten Lwaxana Troi.
ds9-1x18: A telepathic relic of the extinct Saltah'na makes the senior staff replay its creators' power struggle, and only an unaffected Odo can head off Kira's mutiny.
ds9-1x19: Kira's investigation of a Cardassian claiming to be Gallitep's commandant reveals Marritza, a guilt-racked clerk who wants to be executed so Cardassia must face its crimes.
ds9-1x20: Vedek Winn inflames Bajorans against Keiko's secular lessons on the wormhole, and the bombing of her school proves cover for a plot to kill the reformist Vedek Bareil.
ds9-2x01: Kira and O'Brien spring resistance legend Li Nalas from a Cardassian prison camp, only to find his heroism was a fluke, as the xenophobic Circle rises on Bajor.
ds9-2x02: Relieved of her post, Kira retreats to Bareil's monastery and is abducted by the Circle, whose hidden leader is Minister Jaro, as Sisko learns Cardassia is arming it.
ds9-2x03: Sisko's crew fights Circle troops for the station, Li Nalas dies shielding Sisko, and Kira and Dax fly an old raider to Bajor with proof of Cardassia's role.
ds9-2x04: Verad, a Trill deemed unfit for joining, seizes the nearly empty station and forces Bashir to move the Dax symbiont into him, leaving Jadzia hours from death.
ds9-2x05: The case of Rugal, a Cardassian orphan raised by Bajorans, leads Garak and Bashir to a plot by Gul Dukat to disgrace the boy's politician father.
ds9-2x06: Bashir romances Elaysian ensign Melora Pazlar and devises a treatment letting her walk in normal gravity, which she finally declines, as a vengeful ex-partner stalks Quark.
ds9-2x07: Quark negotiates a tulaberry wine deal with the Dosi for Zek, helped by his new aide Pel, a Ferengi woman in male disguise who has fallen for him.
ds9-2x08: An attack on Quark reopens Odo's first murder case from the Occupation, when Dukat drafted him as investigator, and leads him to learn that Kira was the killer.
ds9-2x09: On the anniversary of his wife's death, Sisko falls for the elusive Fenna, who proves to be a telepathic projection of Nidell, the unhappy wife of a terraformer.
ds9-2x10: Skrreean refugees led by Haneek arrive via the wormhole believing Bajor is Kentanna, their prophesied homeland, but the struggling Bajorans turn them away, with tragic results.
ds9-2x11: El-Aurian con man Martus Mazur opens a rival bar with a gambling device that warps probability across the station, as O'Brien becomes fixated on beating Bashir at racquetball.
ds9-2x12: Odo's old mentor Dr. Mora Pol finds a lead on Odo's people, but a creature stalking the station proves to be Odo himself, changed by volcanic gas.
ds9-2x13: After helping the T'Lani and Kellerun destroy their bioweapons, O'Brien and Bashir are hunted by both governments, who want no one alive who knows how the weapons worked.
ds9-2x14: Back from the Parada system, O'Brien grows convinced his crewmates are conspiring against him, never suspecting he is a Paradan replicant built to sabotage peace talks.
ds9-2x15: Stranded on a colony where no technology works, Sisko endures a punishment box while O'Brien exposes Alixus, the leader who secretly created the field trapping everyone.
ds9-2x16: Investigating disappearances in a Gamma Quadrant village, Odo and Dax learn its residents are holograms kept by a lonely exile from the Dominion, and Odo befriends a girl.
ds9-2x17: While mentoring Trill initiate Arjin, Dax finds a tiny, swelling protouniverse that may hold life, and the crew must return it before it consumes the Bajoran system.
ds9-2x18: Quark's old flame Natima Lang arrives as a fugitive Cardassian dissident, and he schemes to win her back and smuggle her out, with surprising help from Garak.
ds9-2x19: Kang, Kor, and Koloth invoke Curzon's blood oath against the Albino, killer of their sons, and Jadzia joins a raid in which the Albino, Kang, and Koloth die.
ds9-2x20: The bombing of a Cardassian freighter leads Sisko to the Maquis, Federation settlers fighting back in the Demilitarized Zone, whose ranks include his old friend Cal Hudson.
ds9-2x21: Sisko recovers the kidnapped Dukat, exposes Cardassian arms smuggling in the zone, and faces down his friend Cal Hudson to keep a Maquis strike from igniting war.
ds9-2x22: Bashir treats Garak for a failing Obsidian Order implant he has abused like a drug, hears three conflicting tales of his exile, and turns to Enabran Tain.
ds9-2x23: A wormhole mishap strands Kira and Bashir in the mirror universe, where humans are slaves, Kira's ruthless double runs the station, and their escape sparks a Terran revolt.
ds9-2x24: Kira probes claims that Bareil betrayed a resistance cell and finds Kai Opaka did it; to shield Opaka's legacy, Bareil withdraws from the Kai race and Winn wins.
ds9-2x25: Seized on vacation, O'Brien faces a rigged Cardassian show trial for aiding the Maquis, until Odo and Sisko expose the frame-up behind it.
ds9-2x26: Sisko's Gamma Quadrant outing with Jake, Nog, and Quark ends with capture by the Jem'Hadar, enforcers of the Dominion, whose suicide run destroys the rescuing USS Odyssey.
ds9-3x01: With the warship Defiant, Sisko ventures into the Gamma Quadrant to find the Dominion's rulers, and Odo, drawn to the Omarion Nebula, finally finds his people.
ds9-3x02: Odo learns his people are the Dominion's Founders, as Sisko watches the Federation accept a ruinous peace deal, a scenario that turns out to be the Founders' test.
ds9-3x03: Quark's bogus boast of killing a Klingon gets him abducted and wed by the widow Grilka, and on Qo'noS his ledgers save her house from the scheming D'Ghor.
ds9-3x04: Haunting visions send Jadzia to Trill, where Sisko and Bashir uncover a host the Symbiosis Commission erased from Dax's record: Joran, a musician and murderer.
ds9-3x05: The Obsidian Order abducts Kira and insists she is Iliana Ghemor, a surgically altered sleeper agent, in a ploy to unmask her supposed father as a dissident.
ds9-3x06: Salvage bought by Quark holds an infant that grows within days into a Jem'Hadar soldier, and Odo tries to raise him beyond his programming before letting him go.
ds9-3x07: A forgotten Cardassian anti-riot program, triggered by accident, treats the station as seized by Bajoran rebels and locks it down ever tighter, trapping even Dukat.
ds9-3x08: Jadzia falls for Deral of Meridian, a planet that drops out of normal space for sixty-year spans, as Quark schemes to sell a holosuite likeness of Kira.
ds9-3x09: Posing as his transporter twin Will, Thomas Riker hijacks the Defiant for the Maquis, and Sisko joins Dukat to hunt him as he uncovers an Obsidian Order fleet.
ds9-3x10: During the Bajoran Gratitude Festival, Lwaxana Troi's Zanthi fever sets off mismatched passions across the station, from Jake's crush on Kira to Bareil's sudden pursuit of Dax.
ds9-3x11: A transporter mishap strands Sisko, Bashir, and Dax in 2024 San Francisco, where Gabriel Bell, a pivotal figure of history, dies saving Sisko, who must take his place.
ds9-3x12: As Gabriel Bell, Sisko sees the Bell Riots through to their historic end, risking his life to shield hostages, while Kira and O'Brien search through time for them.
ds9-3x13: Bashir sustains a dying Vedek Bareil with artificial brain implants so he can steer Kai Winn's peace talks with Cardassia, even as the man himself fades away.
ds9-3x14: A crystal engulfing Kira on a moon prompts Odo to confess his love, and her reply exposes her as the Female Changeling; Nog seeks Sisko's backing for Starfleet.
ds9-3x15: Vedek Yarka warns a doomsday prophecy is unfolding as Cardassian scientists help Sisko build a communications relay through the wormhole, and the omens come true in unexpected ways.
ds9-3x16: Zek returns preaching charity from a rewritten Rules of Acquisition, so Quark hauls him to the Prophets to undo it, while Bashir frets over a Carrington Award nomination.
ds9-3x17: Radiation sends O'Brien skipping hours ahead in time, where he sees his death and the station's destruction, and he must expose a Romulan plot to collapse the wormhole.
ds9-3x18: A Lethean's telepathic assault leaves Bashir comatose in a dreamscape of the station, where he ages by decades and his crewmates embody pieces of his own mind.
ds9-3x19: Abducted into the mirror universe to pose as his dead counterpart, Sisko must turn Jennifer's double, a scientist aiding the Alliance, to the Terran rebels' cause.
ds9-3x20: The bombing of Garak's shop, which Garak staged himself, leads Odo to Enabran Tain and a secret Romulan-Cardassian fleet poised to strike the Founders' homeworld.
ds9-3x21: Back in Tain's service, Garak interrogates Odo as the Romulan-Cardassian fleet attacks the Founders' world and meets a Dominion ambush, and Sisko defies orders to save them.
ds9-3x22: Recreating an ancient Bajoran solar-sail ship, Sisko and Jake ride tachyon eddies all the way to Cardassia, proving that early Bajorans could have made the voyage.
ds9-3x23: Liquidator Brunt shutters Quark's bar until Quark returns to Ferenginar to deal with his mother, Ishka, who has illegally earned profit; Jake sets Sisko up with Kasidy Yates.
ds9-3x24: Ordered by Winn to seize farm equipment from Shakaar, her old resistance leader, Kira joins him instead, and the standoff ends with Shakaar unseating Winn as First Minister.
ds9-3x25: In the Trill zhian'tara rite, Jadzia meets her past hosts through her friends' bodies, confronting the murderous Joran and a Curzon who, housed in Odo, refuses to leave.
ds9-3x26: Sisko's first mission as captain is a trap: the ambassador aboard the Defiant is a Changeling bent on sparking a war, and Odo kills one of his own.
ds9-4x01-02: Recruited by Sisko to probe a Klingon fleet's arrival, Worf uncovers an invasion of Cardassia that shatters the Khitomer Accords and brings a Klingon assault on the station.
ds9-4x03: An elderly Jake recounts how an accident left his father unstuck in time, surfacing briefly across the decades, and how Jake gave his life to set things right.
ds9-4x04: Captured by Jem'Hadar deserters, Bashir tries to free them from their ketracel-white addiction while O'Brien works to escape, and on the station Worf clashes with Odo over Quark.
ds9-4x05: Searching with Dukat for the lost prison ship Ravinok, Kira learns he is after his half-Bajoran daughter Ziyal, whom he plans to kill before relenting.
ds9-4x06: Lenara Kahn, whose symbiont was wed to a past Dax host, rekindles a romance with Jadzia that ends when she refuses to break the Trill taboo against reassociation.
ds9-4x07: Hiding in a gas giant after defending a Karemma ship, the crippled Defiant stalks the Jem'Hadar while Kira keeps a wounded Sisko awake and Worf learns to lead.
ds9-4x08: Flying Nog to Starfleet Academy, Quark and Rom, with Odo stowed away, are thrown back to 1947 Roswell, where the U.S. military takes the Ferengi for alien invaders.
ds9-4x09: Kor, Worf, and Dax recover the Sword of Kahless from a Gamma Quadrant world, but it sets the Klingons against each other, so Worf beams it into space.
ds9-4x10: A transporter emergency stores the senior staff inside Bashir's 1960s spy holosuite fantasy, and he and Garak must play the story out without killing their friends.
ds9-4x11: After a Changeling bombing on Earth, Sisko returns to San Francisco to lead Starfleet security under Admiral Leyton, and a planetwide blackout pushes the president toward emergency rule.
ds9-4x12: Sisko learns the blackout was sabotage by Red Squad cadets serving Admiral Leyton, and races to stop the admiral's coup to put Earth under martial law.
ds9-4x13: Guarding First Minister Shakaar from assassins, Odo watches Kira fall for the man, and his hidden heartbreak leaves him smashing his quarters and nearly failing at his job.
ds9-4x14: Disgraced for acknowledging his half-Bajoran daughter, Dukat ferries Kira to a conference the Klingons destroy, and the two capture a Bird-of-Prey that Dukat turns to his own war.
ds9-4x15: Disgraced by Worf's stand against Gowron, Kurn begs his brother to kill him, and Worf ultimately has Kurn's memories erased so he can start a new life.
ds9-4x16: Rom unionizes Quark's staff and leads them on strike over wages and conditions, defying Quark and the FCA's Brunt, then quits to become a station engineer.
ds9-4x17: Legendary poet Akorem Laan emerges from the wormhole claiming to be the Emissary, and after he revives Bajor's caste system, Sisko reclaims the role he never wanted.
ds9-4x18: Klingon advocate Ch'Pok seeks Worf's extradition after the Defiant, under his command, destroys a civilian transport, until Odo proves its passengers were already dead.
ds9-4x19: The Argrathi punish O'Brien with false memories of two decades behind bars, and back home, guilt over killing his cellmate Ee'Char nearly drives him to suicide.
ds9-4x20: The mirror Jennifer lures Jake across universes to draw Sisko into helping the Terran rebels finish their own Defiant, which he commands against the Regent Worf's fleet.
ds9-4x21: The alluring Onaya inspires Jake's first novel while feeding on his life force, and a pregnant Lwaxana Troi weds Odo to keep her son from his Tavnian father.
ds9-4x22: Sisko faces evidence that Kasidy Yates smuggles for the Maquis, but the deeper betrayal is Lieutenant Eddington's, as he steals a cargo of industrial replicators and defects.
ds9-4x23: After renegade Jem'Hadar raid the station, Sisko forms an uneasy alliance with the Vorta Weyoun and his loyal soldiers to destroy an Iconian gateway the rebels have seized.
ds9-4x24: Bashir's attempt to cure a Dominion-engineered blight on a Gamma Quadrant world fails, but it yields a vaccine that lets the next generation be born healthy.
ds9-4x25: Wrongly told he is dying, Quark sells his remains, then learns the buyer is Brunt, who expects delivery, while Kira carries the O'Briens' baby after an accident.
ds9-4x26: A Founder-induced illness brings Odo to the Great Link, where he is punished for killing a changeling by being made human, and comes away believing Gowron is one.
ds9-5x01: Disguised as Klingons, Sisko's team infiltrates a Klingon stronghold to unmask Gowron as a Changeling, only to discover the impostor is actually General Martok.
ds9-5x02: Holding a crashed Jem'Hadar ship against the Vorta Kilana's siege, Sisko loses crewman Muniz, then learns her real prize was a Founder dying inside the wreck.
ds9-5x03: Worf coaches Quark in Klingon courtship to win back his ex-wife Grilka, even fighting a duel for him by remote control, and ends up falling for Jadzia himself.
ds9-5x04: Traveling with Bashir, Jake lands at a field hospital under Klingon siege on Ajilon Prime, panics and flees under fire, and writes an honest account of his fear.
ds9-5x05: Possessing Keiko, a Pah-wraith forces O'Brien to rig the station to fire on the wormhole and kill the Prophets, until he and Rom turn the plan against it.
ds9-5x06: Klingon spy Arne Darvin drags the Defiant to 2268 to kill Kirk on Space Station K-7, and the crew blends into history, tribbles and all, to stop him.
ds9-5x07: A vacation on Risa goes sour for Worf and Dax when Worf, bristling at the planet's indulgence, joins the Essentialists, a movement plotting to sabotage its weather control.
ds9-5x08: Odo, Sisko, Dax, and Garak wake on Occupation-era Terok Nor as Bajorans condemned to death, an illusion that forces Odo to confront an execution he once allowed.
ds9-5x09: Stranded on a barren world by a bomb, Quark and Odo must haul each other up a mountain to call for help, while Nog moves in with Jake.
ds9-5x10: Visions triggered by an accident lead Sisko to the lost city of B'hala and warn him Bajor must not yet join the Federation, but they are killing him.
ds9-5x11: As her old Shakaar comrades are murdered one by one, a pregnant Kira tracks the killer, a scarred Cardassian who blames her for the innocents her bombs harmed.
ds9-5x12: Odo raises a fragile infant Changeling and makes peace with Dr. Mora, and the dying baby's merger with Odo restores his shape-shifting, as Kira delivers the O'Briens' son.
ds9-5x13: When Maquis turncoat Michael Eddington poisons a Cardassian colony, an obsessed Sisko retaliates by poisoning a Maquis world to force his surrender.
ds9-5x14: Following a coded signal, Garak and Worf land in a Dominion prison camp with Tain, the real Martok, and the real Bashir, whose station double is a Changeling.
ds9-5x15: Dukat leads Cardassia into the Dominion as its fleet emerges, a Changeling posing as Bashir tries to destroy Bajor's sun, and Worf and Garak lead a camp breakout.
ds9-5x16: Lewis Zimmerman models a new medical hologram on Bashir, exposing Julian's secret, illegal genetic enhancement as a child, and his father accepts prison to save his son's career.
ds9-5x17: Odo falls for Arissa, a woman marked for death by the Orion Syndicate, and finds his first love, only to lose her to the family she left behind.
ds9-5x18: Deep in debt, Quark joins his cousin Gaila's arms-dealing business, but when a deal would arm a genocidal regent, his conscience drives him to sabotage it.
ds9-5x19: Kira nurses her dying surrogate father, the Cardassian dissident Tekeny Ghemor, as Dukat and Weyoun press for his extradition and she confronts memories of her own father's death.
ds9-5x20: Home on Ferenginar, Quark finds his mother Ishka romancing Zek and, bribed by Brunt, splits them up, then learns she has been secretly guiding the failing Nagus.
ds9-5x21: As first officer of the demoralized Rotarran, Worf goads a shaken Martok into a duel to restore his nerve, and earns a place in the House of Martok.
ds9-5x22: The Defiant crew meets its 8,000 descendants, born of a crash into the past still ahead of them, and an elder Odo seals their fate for Kira's sake.
ds9-5x23: Sisko drags the jailed Eddington along to find Maquis missiles aimed at Cardassia, but the launch is a bluff to save Maquis survivors, and Eddington dies protecting them.
ds9-5x24: Salvaging parts from Empok Nor, DS9's abandoned twin, O'Brien's team is picked off by drug-crazed Cardassian soldiers, and when the drug infects Garak, O'Brien must outwit him.
ds9-5x25: Hoping to cheer Sisko, Jake and Nog trade favors across the station to land a 1951 Willie Mays card, while Weyoun offers Bajor a nonaggression pact.
ds9-5x26: Sisko seals the wormhole with self-replicating mines, and when Dukat's fleet retakes the station, Starfleet withdraws, leaving Kira, Odo, and Quark behind as Sisko vows to return.
ds9-6x01: With the war going badly, Sisko takes a captured Jem'Hadar ship behind enemy lines to destroy the Dominion's ketracel-white depot, while Kira and Odo live uneasily under occupation.
ds9-6x02: Stranded on an ocean world, Sisko's crew faces Jem'Hadar short of ketracel-white whose Vorta sells them out, and a Bajoran's suicide spurs Kira to resist the Dominion.
ds9-6x03: Worf's son Alexander enlists on the Rotarran, forcing father and son to confront their past, while Dukat uses Ziyal's return to Terok Nor to draw closer to Kira.
ds9-6x04: The Female Changeling draws Odo into linking with her as Kira's resistance cell needs him to thwart the Dominion's plan to clear the minefield, and Rom is captured.
ds9-6x05: Sisko persuades Starfleet to mount a fleet to retake the station before the minefield falls, while a captured Rom faces execution and Kira's cell fights to free him.
ds9-6x06: Sisko's Defiant punches through the Dominion lines alone, the Prophets make an entire enemy armada vanish in the wormhole at a price, and Ziyal's death shatters Dukat.
ds9-6x07: Worf and Jadzia move up their wedding, but Martok's wife Sirella objects to the bride, and the ordeal of Klingon rites nearly ends the marriage before it begins.
ds9-6x08: The mirror universe's Bareil arrives seeking refuge and wins Kira's heart, but he is a thief working with the Intendant to steal a Bajoran Orb.
ds9-6x09: Bashir enlists a band of genetically enhanced misfits to analyze enemy data, but their projections lead them to urge surrender and try to leak secrets to the Dominion.
ds9-6x10: To ransom his captured mother, Quark assembles a Ferengi crew, Brunt included, to swap the Vorta Keevan for her on Empok Nor, a plan that soon goes awry.
ds9-6x11: After the Honshu is destroyed, an injured Sisko is stranded with a deranged Dukat, whose hallucinated arguments peel away his self-justifications until he embraces his hatred of Bajorans.
ds9-6x12: Morn's apparent death leaves Quark his estate, drawing Morn's former partners, who want a share of latinum from an old heist, until Morn turns out to be alive.
ds9-6x13: The Prophets cast Sisko as Benny Russell, a Black writer in 1950s New York whose tale of a Black space station captain his editors refuse to print.
ds9-6x14: Shrunk with their runabout while studying a spatial anomaly, Dax, O'Brien, and Bashir must fly inside the Defiant's circuitry to help Sisko retake it from Jem'Hadar boarders.
ds9-6x15: Undercover in the Orion Syndicate for Starfleet Intelligence, O'Brien grows close to Bilby, a small-time crook, and must betray him to stop a Dominion-backed assassination.
ds9-6x16: Worf abandons a mission on Soukara to save a gravely wounded Jadzia, a choice that may cost him his career, as O'Brien and Bashir tackle Quark at tongo.
ds9-6x17: Stung by Dukat's claim about her mother, Kira steps through the Orb of Time into the Occupation and learns Meru became his mistress to keep her family alive.
ds9-6x18: Accused of spying for the Dominion by the investigator Sloan, Bashir learns the ordeal was a test by Section 31, a covert Starfleet body eager to recruit him.
ds9-6x19: Sisko has Garak forge evidence to pull Romulus into the war; when the forgery is caught, Garak murders Senator Vreenak, and Sisko concludes he can live with it.
ds9-6x20: Vic Fontaine, a self-aware holographic lounge singer, coaches Odo in romance, and after a mix-up with a holographic stand-in, Odo finally tells Kira he loves her.
ds9-6x21: An ancient tablet from B'hala heralds the Reckoning, in which a Prophet inhabits Kira and a Pah-wraith seizes Jake, until Kai Winn halts the battle.
ds9-6x22: Rescued by the Valiant, a warship crewed by Red Squad cadets, Jake and Nog watch its zealous captain lead it into a doomed attack on a Dominion battleship.
ds9-6x23: Zek is ousted as Nagus for backing women's rights, and to keep Brunt from taking over, Quark briefly becomes a woman, Lumba, to win over the influential Nilva.
ds9-6x24: Retrieved from a time portal on Golana as a feral eighteen-year-old, Molly O'Brien cannot adjust, and her parents make a wrenching choice to restore her childhood.
ds9-6x25: The Defiant crew bonds by radio with Captain Lisa Cusak, stranded on a hostile planet, only to arrive and find a time distortion meant she died years before.
ds9-6x26: Brushing aside the Prophets' warning, Sisko commands the Federation offensive at Chin'toka, while Dukat, possessed by a Pah-wraith, kills Jadzia and closes the wormhole.
ds9-7x01: Grieving in New Orleans, Sisko follows a vision to the secret of his real mother, Sarah, as Worf seeks a glorious battle to send Jadzia's spirit to Sto-Vo-Kor.
ds9-7x02: Sisko finds the Orb of the Emissary and reopens the wormhole, Worf's team hits a Dominion shipyard, Kira blockades the Romulans, and Ezri Dax arrives.
ds9-7x03: Newly joined and unsure of herself, Ezri Dax becomes the station's counselor and helps Garak through a breakdown rooted in guilt over betraying Cardassia, while Worf resents her.
ds9-7x04: Goaded by his old Vulcan rival Solok, Sisko drills his inept crew into a baseball team, and they lose to the Logicians but celebrate a single hard-won run.
ds9-7x05: Bashir brings Sarina, the catatonic member of the genetically enhanced group, into full awareness, then falls in love with her before realizing she needs time to find herself.
ds9-7x06: A flawed Weyoun clone defects to Odo, revealing the Founders are dying of a disease, as Nog trusts the Great Material Continuum to find O'Brien a spare part.
ds9-7x07: Aging warrior Kor seeks one last battle, but Martok, who bears an old grudge, blocks him, until Kor takes on a suicide mission to cover the fleet's retreat.
ds9-7x08: Delivering supplies to AR-558, a captured Dominion relay held by exhausted Starfleet troops, Sisko's crew stays to defend it against a Jem'Hadar assault, and Nog loses his leg.
ds9-7x09: Abducted to Empok Nor, Kira finds Dukat leading a Bajoran Pah-wraith cult and unmasks him when he orders a mass suicide he secretly means to survive.
ds9-7x10: Traumatized by the loss of his leg, Nog hides in Vic Fontaine's 1962 Las Vegas, until Vic realizes he must push his friend back to his real life.
ds9-7x11: To find a missing O'Brien, Ezri goes home to her domineering mother's mining company on New Sydney and uncovers her brother Norvo's role in a murder.
ds9-7x12: The Klingon-Cardassian Alliance of the mirror universe kidnaps Grand Nagus Zek, and its ransom forces Quark and Rom to steal the Defiant's cloaking device and cross over.
ds9-7x13: To catch a sniper whose rifle fires through walls, Ezri calls up the persona of Joran, Dax's murderous past host, and learns to think like a killer.
ds9-7x14: Laas, a fellow Changeling sent out as an infant like Odo, urges him to abandon solids, and after he kills a Klingon, Kira frees him for Odo's sake.
ds9-7x15: When mobster Frankie Eyes seizes Vic's lounge through a hidden program twist, the crew plots a casino heist to set things right, and a reluctant Sisko joins in.
ds9-7x16: At a conference on Romulus, Bashir is used in Sloan's Section 31 plot, which frames Senator Cretak and puts Section 31's secret ally Koval on the Continuing Committee.
ds9-7x17: Sisko proposes to Kasidy, Ezri finds a stranded Worf and sleeps with him before the Breen capture them both, and Dukat is surgically disguised as a Bajoran.
ds9-7x18: Sisko weds Kasidy despite the Prophets' warning, a disguised Dukat becomes the guide Kai Winn believes she was promised, and the Breen interrogate Worf and Ezri.
ds9-7x19: The Dominion signs a treaty with the Breen that costs Cardassia territory, stoking Damar's resentment, as Worf and Ezri await execution and Winn chooses to follow the Pah-wraiths.
ds9-7x20: Breen raids hit Earth and a new energy-draining weapon destroys the Defiant, while Damar launches a Cardassian rebellion and Winn turns to forbidden Pah-wraith texts.
ds9-7x21: Kira, commissioned a Starfleet commander, goes with Odo and Garak to advise Damar's rebels, Bashir finds Odo carries the Founders' disease, and Gowron seizes command from Martok.
ds9-7x22: Gowron's reckless war drives Worf to kill him in combat and make Martok chancellor, while Kira, Damar, and Garak steal a Breen energy-dampening weapon.
ds9-7x23: Desperate to cure Odo, Bashir and O'Brien lure Section 31's Sloan to the station and enter his dying mind to steal the cure hidden in his memories.
ds9-7x24: The Dominion crushes Damar's rebellion, forcing Kira, Damar, and Garak into hiding on Cardassia, as Quark expects to be named Grand Nagus until Zek chooses Rom.
ds9-7x25-26: Allies storm Cardassia and Odo's link with the Female Changeling ends the war, while Sisko thwarts Winn and Dukat's bid to free the Pah-wraiths and joins the Prophets.
ent-1x01-02: Earth's first warp-five starship, Enterprise, launches early under Captain Archer to return a wounded Klingon courier home, and runs into the Suliban Cabal and a temporal cold war.
ent-1x03: Enterprise finds an Axanar ship whose crew has been drained of a valuable fluid, and a doubting Hoshi Sato must master the Axanar language when the killers return.
ent-1x04: Camping on the first Earth-like planet Enterprise finds, the landing party is exposed to hallucinogenic pollen, and a paranoid Trip becomes convinced T'Pol is plotting with rock creatures.
ent-1x05: Helping repair a stalled Xyrillian ship, Trip Tucker plays a mental game with its engineer Ah'Len and returns pregnant, sending Archer to the Klingons for help finding her.
ent-1x06: At Terra Nova, Earth's first colony, silent for decades, Enterprise finds survivors' descendants underground, blaming Earth for poisoned rain that actually came from an asteroid strike.
ent-1x07: Visiting the Vulcan monastery at P'Jem, Archer's party is taken hostage by Andorians under Shran, who insist it hides a spy post, and Archer finds they are right.
ent-1x08: Shadowed by a Vulcan ship, Enterprise sends Reed and Mayweather to sample a comet, where a mishap strands their shuttlepod, while Trip learns of T'Pol's arranged marriage.
